items.title: [Bug] Intermittent SAPIEN render hangs on RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell during RoboTwin evaluation
items.body:
## Environment

- OS: Ubuntu 24.04.3 LTS
- GPU: NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell Workstation Edition, 96 GB
- NVIDIA driver: 580.159.03
- CUDA runtime: 12.8
- Python: 3.10
- PyTorch: 2.7.1+cu128
- SAPIEN: 3.0.0b1
- Benchmark/evaluator: RoboTwin-compatible DOMINO evaluation environment
- DOMINO source revision: `93d485a34a6e710bb4c895d83e2bb0520a9f169e`

## Bug description

During long RoboTwin policy evaluations, some seeds intermittently hang inside the SAPIEN/Vulkan/rendering or simulator C/CUDA path. The Python process remains alive, but no new log output is produced for a long time and no Python exception is raised. Other seeds in the same task can complete normally, and restarting the task process allows evaluation to continue.

This is reproducible across multiple tasks/seeds. In one `adjust_bottle / demo_clean_dynamic` run, the following seeds timed out after making partial progress:

- seed `4300034`, around step `94 / 400`
- seed `4300027`, around step `110 / 400`
- seed `4300003`, around step `36 / 400`
- seed `4300005`, around step `16 / 400`

The external watchdog terminated the owned process after 1200 seconds without log progress. The evaluation then continued with a new process. In the same run, other seeds completed successfully, so this does not look like a deterministic policy exception.

## Reproduction

1. Run a RoboTwin/DOMINO evaluation with one persistent evaluator process over many seeds, for example `adjust_bottle`, `demo_clean_dynamic`, 100 episodes.
2. Use the standard SAPIEN renderer and no per-episode video encoding.
3. Let the evaluator run through multiple scene resets.
4. Observe that a seed can stop producing output while the Python process and GPU context remain alive.

The issue also occurs with the following mitigations enabled:

- `clear_cache_freq: 1`
- ray-tracing denoiser disabled (`set_ray_tracing_denoiser("none")`)
- replay/environment video saving disabled
- a single evaluator process on an otherwise idle GPU

With the denoiser disabled, the OIDN error messages disappear, but the intermittent SAPIEN/rendering hang still occurs.

## Related issues and attempted fixes

- RoboTwin #83: removing the `assets/objects/objaverse/pencil` asset appears to avoid some slow scenes, but the reason is unclear and this is not a general fix.
- RoboTwin #191 and #198: OIDN errors remain open issues.
- SAPIEN #243: upgrading the bundled OIDN libraries from 2.0.1 to 2.3.3 is reported to fix OIDN errors on RTX 5090, but it does not address the observed no-output SAPIEN hang, and it is not an official SAPIEN/RoboTwin package update.
- RoboTwin PR #453: cache/resource cleanup was merged, but the hang still occurs with `clear_cache_freq: 1`.

## Questions

1. Is RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell supported with SAPIEN 3.0.0b1 and RoboTwin ray-tracing evaluation?
2. Is there a recommended SAPIEN version, NVIDIA driver, CUDA version, or OIDN package combination for Blackwell workstation GPUs?
3. Is there an official way to disable the problematic renderer/denoiser path while preserving the benchmark observation protocol?
4. Are there known scene/object combinations beyond `pencil` that trigger this hang?
5. Should RoboTwin add an official per-episode process isolation/timeout and deterministic infrastructure-failure ledger instead of silently skipping the affected seed?

A maintainer-confirmed minimal workaround or a patched upstream version would be very helpful.

items.title: [python] Avoid importing optional solvers during availability checks
items.body:
## Description

  `available_solvers()` currently imports CVXPY and qpOASES to determine whether they are available. Importing these optional dependencies can add noticeable startup latency, particularly on resource-constrained platforms such as NVIDIA Jetson.
  This change uses `importlib.util.find_spec()` to detect whether the optional solver packages are installed without importing them.
  The actual solver imports remain in their solver-specific code paths and are only performed when those solvers are used.

  ## Changes

  - Detect `cvxpy` using `importlib.util.find_spec("cvxpy")`.
  - Detect `qpoases` using `importlib.util.find_spec("qpoases")`.
  - Preserve the existing availability results for both `qpoases` and `hotqpoases`.
  - Add a regression test that fails if `available_solvers()` imports either optional dependency.
  - Allow the regression test to run through both pytest and direct Python execution.

result.body:
The out-of-memory is actually due to exhaustion of fences. The message by Vulkan is a bit misleading. The driver is simply saying it cannot create more fences. For each camera, SAPIEN will create a fence to synchronize its work. When creating many cameras across many processes, it seems to hit a limit of the maximum fences that can be created system-wide defined by the driver.
While we do not have a workaround for this issue, in SAPIEN 3 and ManiSkill3, we have introduced GPU-batched camera that allows running many cameras at once sharing the same fence. Simulating and rendering everything in the same process (even on the same GPU) is also much more efficient than ManiSKill2 (often 10-100x faster), so that is now the recommended way to use batched environments. If you would like to switch to ManiSkill3, you can find the documentation here https://maniskill.readthedocs.io/en/latest/user_guide/ 

For the frozen issue, I cannot really tell what is causing it. I may be able to take a look if you can reproduce it with pure SAPIEN code. SimplerEnv seems to be on top of ManiSkill2, which is 2 layers of encapsulations from SAPIEN and many things could go wrong.

@XYZ-99 since you are using SIMPLER I am still migrating that over to ManiSkill 3 so you can't quite use the new system yet. Hopefully I will have some example environments in SIMPLER ported over to the GPU sim + rendering system for faster batched evaluation, currently only have some of the CPU side of things done.

@fbxiang Thank you for your timely response!
1. "The out-of-memory is actually due to exhaustion of fences." Then it is strange enough that when I run the same script multiple times with a fixed number of environments, this error sometimes occurs but sometimes doesn't.
2. Also, if the fence is used to "synchronize", it seems suspicious to me if my "stuck" problem arises from a deadlock when the processes try to synchronize.
I will do more investigation and share any information that I think might be helpful to you to identify the problem.
3. Thank you for the reminder of the release of ManiSkill3! However, since my use case is mostly in SIMPLER, it might be non-trivial to myself how to migrate SIMPLER to ManiSkill3.

I actually partially migrated SIMPLER just yesterday. See this for how to access the parallelized simpler environments (only bridge dataset atm) and how to run inference fast on it: https://maniskill.readthedocs.io/en/latest/tasks/digital_twins/index.html#bridgedata-v2-evaluation

Runs about 60-100x faster than real world evaluation speed, 10x faster than CPU sim (and higher if you have a good gpu)

Google robot is complicated because it uses ruckig originally for the controller. I don't know if there exists a GPU parallelized version of the google robot controller out there, so someone would need to write cuda / pytorch code to imitate that controllers behavior. This is the hardest part and why I avoided adding google robot tasks for now.

It's possible but not trivial. As a result the timeline is uncertain. However there is also a possibility one can approximate the controller using existing maniskill controllers and tuning them heavily. I haven't investigated this deeply though.

It is currently easier now to add new environments for robots that use existing controllers (like pd joint delta pos, or ik based ones that control the end effector like the robot in bridge dataset)

Got it! It sounds non-trivial to take advantage of the GPU-parallelization for google robot then.
I still highly appreciate your work on bridge and I look forward to your any forthcoming update on ManiSkill!
